correctness.rationale: The Luce exponential race gives independent Exp(a_i) exceptional scaled clocks and a unit Poisson limit for the ordinary clock point process. Given exceptional ranks the ordinary labels are exactly uniform over n-m positions; the falling-factorial moments are (h)_k/(n-m)_k with n-2m<=h<=n-m. Uniform generating-series domination establishes independent Poisson(1) ordinary fixed points. A memoryless exponential competition yields the exact m-step generating-polynomial recursion. Hypergeometric rectangle concentration establishes the Lebesgue permuton. For arbitrary one-spike weights the first-rank probability is exactly w_n/(w_n+n-1). The standalone exact-rational verifier passes 1031 cases, including exhaustive small permutations, conditional moments, recursion coefficients and asymptotic numerical cross-checks; these are supplemental to, not replacements for, the general proof.

value.rationale: A documented open question conjectures fixed-point Poisson behavior based on the permuton diagonal. This theorem exhibits a naturally scaled rare preferred-item perturbation that preserves the uniform permuton yet changes the fixed-point limit, quantifies the critical weight scale for one preferred item, and gives a finite-state exact correction law for any fixed collection. The phenomenon identifies a concrete boundary for permuton-based inference instead of an arbitrary computation.
